title: ModSRAM: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design for Large Number Modular Multiplication in SRAM
problem: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) computational complexity and memory constraints limit performance, with modular multiplication consuming most processing time and creating a bottleneck between computation and data movement.
motivation: ECC is widely deployed in security-critical applications including public key cryptography and zero-knowledge proofs, making performance improvements in modular multiplication highly valuable.
method: ModSRAM puts computation circuits directly inside SRAM memory chips, so data doesn't need to shuttle back and forth between memory and a separate processor. Instead of computing carries (the numbers you carry over when doing arithmetic), it uses an algorithm called R4CSA-LUT with pre-calculated lookup tables to perform modular multiplication much faster. Because the algorithm and hardware design work together, the same data can be reused multiple times while staying in memory, eliminating wasted trips.
key_novelty: It's the first processor-in-memory architecture using 8T SRAM that speeds up large-number modular multiplication for cryptography.
contributions: ModSRAM: first 8T SRAM PIM architecture for modular multiplication
R4CSA-LUT algorithm eliminating carry propagation via look-up table-based computation
Algorithm-hardware co-design approach for ECC acceleration
52% cycle reduction versus prior works with 32% area overhead
primary_theme: SRAM-based PIM for efficient ECC acceleration
